title: Pointing a tracker at the right thing
target: How to get useful answers out of the valuable tracker in R.E.P.O., given that it is a device you aim rather than a marker you read.
version: R.E.P.O. v0.4.0, as installed for this build (see the sources page for the exact version string)
prerequisites: Something you are trying to find
A moment when the room is quiet enough to listen

steps.do: Aim it rather than holding it up, because it has a nozzle.
steps.because: the tracker has a nozzle with a light of its own (nozzleTransform)

steps.do: Watch the screen as well as listening to it.
steps.because: it carries a display and a text readout (displayText)

steps.do: Learn the found and the lost signals before you rely on it.
steps.because: the game keeps separate sounds and colours for each (soundTargetFound)

steps.do: Use it in the dark, since it lights itself.
steps.because: both the nozzle and the display carry lights (nozzleLight)

steps.do: Treat it as one item among several rather than the only tool.
steps.because: the tracker is one of many carried items (ItemTracker)

commonMistakes: Holding the tracker without pointing it at anything.
Reading the screen and ignoring the sound.
Carrying a tracker instead of something that moves loot.
sources: This installation of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
